Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited. Our legal group attached a first-pass redline for your MSA and the order form focused on two items we need clarified before procurement can approve:

1) Confidentiality carveouts — they want an explicit carveout for aggregated telemetry and for non-personal benchmarking results.

I've attached their redline (CloudPilot_MSA_Redlines_v1.docx). Can you route to legal and advise what Redwood can accept? Also — is there a standard DocuSign flow you prefer if we get to an agreement?

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to close next week.

From: kimberly.park@redwood.com
To: logan.wright@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2026 11:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: MSA review — confidentiality & publicity items

Logan / Marissa — reviewed CloudPilot's redline. Summary and suggested edits below (see also Redwood_Proposed_Publicity_Language.txt attached):

1) Telemetry carveout: we can accept an aggregated/non-identifiable telemetry carveout that permits benchmarking and model performance metrics provided: (a) data is aggregated at >5 customer threshold OR averaged over time windows that prevent re-identification, and (b) no PII or customer-specific configs are included. Suggest language: "Redwood may use aggregated, de-identified service telemetry and anonymized performance metrics for internal product development and for benchmarking, provided that such metrics cannot be reasonably used to identify the Customer or Customer Content."

2) Publicity & press releases: CloudPilot's 30-day review is longer than our standard but acceptable as a one-time concession for strategic deals. We should push to a 10-business-day review SLA for press releases and a 5-business-day window for logo/website references. If CloudPilot insists on 30 days for press releases, propose a hard cap of two review cycles within the 30-day window. Also add clear approval mechanics (printed signoff or email chain) and a mutual right to withdraw the asset within 14 days if confidential information is inadvertently included.

3) Logo scope: restrict to website and product pages, prevent use in third-party press kits or paid advertising without an additional approval step.

4) Implementation: redlines attached as tracked changes. If Sales wants to keep momentum, we can sign a short order-form addendum with the publicity language and ship MSA redline after. But procurement prefers full MSA sign-off.

Action items:
- Marissa: please prepare a DocuSign envelope with the order form and include a short addendum referencing the publicity language.
- Logan: if you agree, I can produce a clean redline to return to CloudPilot with our compromise language.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Proposed_Publicity_Language.txt]

From: logan.wright@redwood.com
To: Sara Mills <sara.mills@cloudpilot.io>, contracts@cloudpilot.io
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA review — confidentiality & publicity items

Hi Sara — thanks for sending the redlines and for the fast turnaround. Looping in legal and sales ops for visibility.

Summary of Redwood's proposed compromise (see attached language):
- Telemetry: Redwood accepts an aggregated, de-identified telemetry carveout for benchmarking and product analytics. We propose the aggregation threshold / anonymization approach Kimberly outlined to avoid any re-identification risk.
- Publicity: We can accept a 30-calendar-day review for press releases as CloudPilot requested, provided there are no more than two review cycles inside that window and that Redwood receives clear written approval (email or signed doc). For logo and website references we request a shorter 5-business-day approval SLA.
- Logo usage: limited to CloudPilot's website and product pages; any third-party press kit or paid ad use will require separate approval.

Next steps:
1) I've attached the proposed publicity language for your review (Redwood_Proposed_Publicity_Language.txt).
2) Marissa will prepare a DocuSign envelope with the order form and an addendum referencing the publicity language; if procurement wants to sign MSA + order form together we can pause the envelope and produce a consolidated DocuSign.

Can you confirm by end of day Thursday whether CloudPilot can accept the limited two-cycle review inside 30 days and the 5-business-day logo approval window? If yes, Marissa will start the DocuSign and we can aim to close this week.

Thanks — excited to get CloudPilot onboard.

Best,
Logan Wright
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
[Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Publicity_Language.txt, DocuSign_Link.txt]
